title: Adjective + to ...
subtitle: hard to understand / nice of you to ... / sorry to hear / the first to ... / bound to ...
summary: Use adjective + to ... to say how easy or hard something is, to judge somebody's behaviour, to describe reactions, and after the first/last/only and sure/likely/bound.

lesson.heading: hard to understand, interesting to talk to

left.label: It is + adjective + to ... + object
examples: Do you think **it is safe to drink** this water?
The exam questions were very hard. **It was impossible to answer them.**
Nicola has lots of interesting ideas. **It's interesting to talk to her.**

right.label: Subject + is + adjective + to ...
right.text: Same meaning. Do not repeat the object at the end.
examples: **He is hard to understand.** (not He is hard to understand him)
Do you think this water **is safe to drink**? (not to drink it)
They **were impossible to answer**. (not to answer them)
Nicola **is interesting to talk to**. (not to talk to her)

lesson.note: Other adjectives used like this: easy, nice, safe, cheap, exciting, impossible, interesting, difficult, good, dangerous, expensive.

lesson.heading: adjective + noun + to ...
lesson.text: We also use this structure with **adjective + noun**: *a difficult question to answer*, *an easy mistake to make*. Again, do not repeat the object.

examples.text: This is **a difficult question to answer**.

lesson.heading: It's nice of you to ...
lesson.text: We say **It's nice of somebody to do something** to judge a person's behaviour. Other adjectives used in the same way: *kind, generous, careless, silly, stupid, inconsiderate, unfair, typical*.

examples.text: **It was nice of you to take** me to the airport. Thank you very much.
**It's silly of Ruth to give up** her job when she needs the money.
I think **it was unfair of him to criticise** me.

lesson.heading: sorry to ... / surprised to ... etc.
lesson.text: You can use **adjective + to ...** to say how somebody reacts to something. Adjectives used like this: *sorry, glad, pleased, relieved, surprised, amazed, sad, disappointed*.

examples.text: I'm **sorry to hear** that your mother isn't well.
It was a long and tiring journey. We were **glad to get** home.

lesson.heading: the first / the next / the last / the only ... to ...
lesson.text: You can use **to ...** after *the next, the last, the only, the first, the second* etc.

examples.text: **The next train to arrive** at platform 4 will be the 10.50 to Liverpool.
Everybody was late except me. I was **the only one to arrive** on time.
If I have any more news, you will be **the first to know**.

lesson.heading: sure / likely / bound to ...
lesson.text: You can say that something is **sure to happen**, **likely to happen** or **bound to happen**. *Bound to* means *sure to*.

examples.text: Carla is a very good student. She's **bound to pass** the exam.
It's possible I'll win the lottery one day, but it's **not likely to happen**.

lesson.text: When the subject of the sentence is the thing being talked about, do not repeat it after the verb: *The water is safe to drink* (not ~~to drink it~~).

exercises.prompt: Nicola has lots of interesting ideas. She is interesting ___.
exercises.explanation: Subject + adjective + to ...: we keep the preposition but do not repeat the object (not to talk to her).

exercises.prompt: It was difficult to open the window. Say the same thing beginning with The window.
exercises.answer: The window was difficult to open.

exercises.statement: This meat isn't safe to eat it.
exercises.explanation: This meat isn't safe to eat. Do not repeat the object after the verb.

exercises.prompt: It's a very common mistake. It's an easy mistake ___.
exercises.explanation: adjective + noun + to ...: an easy mistake to make.

exercises.prompt: It was nice ___ to remember my birthday.
exercises.explanation: We say it's nice of somebody to do something.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern does each adjective take?
categories: It was ... of you to help me.
I was ... to hear the news.

exercises.prompt: I heard about Tom's accident. I was relieved ___ that he's OK.
exercises.explanation: adjective + to ... for a reaction: relieved to hear.

exercises.prompt: My interview went well. I was disappointed ___ to be offered the job.
exercises.explanation: The negative goes before to: disappointed not to be offered the job.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the right ending.

pairs.left: Everybody else arrived before Paul. Paul was ...
Emily passed the exam. All the other students failed. Emily was ...
I complained to the manager. Another customer had already complained. I was ...
Neil Armstrong walked on the moon in 1969. Nobody had done this before him. He was ...
pairs.right: the first man to walk on the moon.

exercises.prompt: I'm not surprised you're tired after your trip. ___ after such a long journey.
answers: You are bound to be tired
exercises.explanation: bound to + verb = sure to: You're bound to be tired.

exercises.prompt: It's easy to get to my house from here. Say the same thing beginning with My house.
exercises.answer: My house is easy to get to from here.

exercises.prompt: I don't think you'll need an umbrella. ___.
answers: It is not likely to rain
exercises.explanation: likely to + verb: It's not likely to rain (= it's not probable).
